Lays a tree out into boxes and draws them. The two halves are public and separate on purpose: a host with a gui of its own can call `layout` to get the boxes, do what it likes with them, and call `paint` to draw them inside whatever it is already drawing.

Layout is arithmetic over a dom tree and needs no running game, which is what lets the whole engine be checked headless.

```java
import net.tutla.craftytml.client.render.CTMLRenderer;
```

## Members

### `public static CTMLLayout.Box renderScreen(DOMTreeElement domTreeHeadElement, Screen screen, GuiGraphicsExtractor graphics)`

### `public static CTMLLayout.Box render(DOMTreeElement domHeadElement, GuiGraphicsExtractor graphics, int viewWidth, int viewHeight)`

### `public static CTMLLayout.Box layout(DOMTreeElement domHeadElement, int viewWidth, int viewHeight)`

Works out where everything goes without drawing any of it, so a screen can keep the answer.

### `public static void paint(CTMLLayout.Box root, GuiGraphicsExtractor graphics)`

Draws a tree that has already been laid out, which is every frame's half of the work.

### `public static void paint(CTMLLayout.Box root, GuiGraphicsExtractor graphics, DOMTreeElement focus)`

The same, with a ring drawn round whatever element has the keyboard.

### `public static List<CTMLLayout.Box> order(CTMLLayout.Box box)`

The order the stacking context a box starts paints in, as the boxes themselves: the box first and then everything under it that does not start a context of its own, sorted the way paint sorts it. A box that does start one stands for the whole of its own context, since nothing inside one is sorted against anything outside it.
